title: Adaptive probe-guided sample pruner and runner shim for lightweight profile generation
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Full-profile runs for model onboarding are expensive and noisy when using large cataloged datasets + many prompt variants. We need an automated pre-sampling stage that quickly identifies representative slices and prunes low-value prompt variants, plus a lightweight evaluation runner shim to reduce per-run overhead for these probe passes.

Goal: Implement a probe-guided sample pruner that: (1) executes fast, low-cost probe runs across dataset shards and prompt clusters; (2) scores variance, failure modes, and model delta sensitivity; (3) produces a compact, prioritized sample set for full profile generation. Additionally, ship a runner shim that starts in a persistable warm state, supports batch-affinity hints, and tolerates quantized model variants so probe runs mirror production performance. This should reduce CI cost for profile generation by >=60% and surface problematic prompts earlier in the onboarding flow.
acceptance_criteria: Probe stage implemented and configurable via harness config with <10s setup time per runner
Pruner outputs deterministic prioritized sample set (seeded) and exposes top-k recommendation
Runner shim reduces per-eval cold-start latency by >=40% in benchmarked scenarios
Integration tests added to harness CI verifying stability across LLM families (decoder-only & chat-style)
Documentation: Confluence design doc, quickstart for PMs/Onboarders, and console UI linkage for generated profile artifacts
Demo: Run on three nightly onboarding candidates and show end-to-end cost reduction in dashboard
technical_notes: Probe design: run 50–200 low-length tokens per shard using quantized variants (4-bit and 8-bit) to estimate sensitivity metrics: token-level perplexity proxy, stop-token rate, top-k entropy and rank stability
Scoring heuristics: combined metric = 0.5 * variance_score + 0.3 * failure_rate + 0.2 * delta_sensitivity. Tunable weights in config
Pruner decisions: remove prompt variants with low delta_sensitivity and low information gain across seed bank; keep out-of-distribution prompts flagged by model confidence drop
Runner shim: lightweight process that reuses a pre-allocated KV cache container, accepts batch-affinity headers, and exposes a /warm-start endpoint to pin model variant and quantization profile
Trade-offs: aggressive pruning reduces CI cost but risks missing rare regressions; mitigation: keep periodic randomized sampling of pruned prompts at a small rate (1-2%)
Backward compatibility: shim must fall back to existing runner interface when affinity headers are absent
Telemetry: emit probe-run metrics: shard_id, probe_latency_ms, variance_score, keep_probability, runner_cold_start_ms
Security: probe runs use redacted customer prompts when running against private datasets; ensure logging respects PII filters

review_feedback: Design review (2026-02-26): Keep scoring weights configurable and add experiment flags to ramp pruning aggressiveness over 3 cycles.
Security review (2026-03-02): Ensure probe telemetry never contains raw prompt text; use hash references and redaction pipeline
Performance review (2026-03-04): Runner shim must expose perf counters via Prometheus and be compatible with existing tracing hooks
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Over-pruning can hide regressions. Mitigation: maintain randomized holdout 1-2% and conservative default keep thresholds
Risk: Runner shim complexity may increase maintenance burden. Mitigation: keep shim tiny, implement via existing runtime library and document clear interfacing

Risk: Quantization mismatch between probe and full-profile runs. Mitigation: include quantization-profile tag in recommendation and optionally run probe with highest-fidelity variant for models flagged as unstable
notes_for_oncall: If harness CI starts failing stable profiles after merge, look at probe_pruner.keep_probability and runner_warm_max_age config — reverting to conservative defaults helps immediate stability
Monitor runtime/kv_cache_bytes and probe-run cold_start_ms after rollout — set alert if cache grows >10% baseline
